item.title: Compute brief - 3 November 2026
item.description: Anthropic amended its S-1 on 3 November with third-quarter revenue of $17 billion and a net loss of $23.29 billion, and its purchase commitments and leases now total about $895.4 billion, substantially all for compute and infrastructure, up from $417 billion previously listed. The filing names $121.3 billion with Google, $120.5 billion with SpaceX, $110 billion with Amazon, $44.9 billion with Microsoft, $44.6 billion with Nscale, $41.3 billion with Lambda and $50 billion with Fluidstack, per DCD. Against last week's neocloud credit squeeze, the supply side is starting to reprice: Crusoe's public price page now shows new on-demand rates from 1 December 2026, with H100 up 15.4% to $4.50, H200 up 25.9% to $5.40 and B300 up 10.5% to $9.90 per GPU-hour. Today's live prints are unchanged, so the tape shows 70 confirms, 0 ticks and 0 NEW; Lambda H100 holds at $3.99 and B200 at $6.69. Countries: United Kingdom: Drax, Brookfield and Radiant plan GW-scale data centre capacity at Drax Power Station; up to 100 MW from Q1 2028, investment could exceed £20 billion (Wire, 3 Nov). Saudi Arabia: Aramco closes a 49% stake in HUMAIN with about $2.6 billion in cash plus assets; 3 GW by 2030 target restated (Wire, 1 Nov). Russia: Putin decree orders private data centres to reserve 10% of space and capacity for state needs, 10 days to comply (Wire, 2 Nov). Malaysia: Google funds $160 million of shared water infrastructure for its planned Port Dickson campus (Wire, 2 Nov). South Korea: KB Kookmin leads about 10.7 trillion won of loans for Brookfield's GPU SPC supplying Naver Cloud (Wire, 1 Nov). United States: Nvidia in talks to guarantee debt for Nscale's 460 MW Anthropic building in West Virginia (Wire, 29 Oct, corroborated).
